paragraphs: Bilevel optimization describes a decision problem whose outcome depends on solving another optimization problem inside it. This paper studies the setting where the inner problem is strongly convex and has coupled linear constraints. Those constraints can make the outer objective nonsmooth, while methods involving Hessian matrices introduce additional computational challenges.

The authors use penalty and augmented Lagrangian methods to replace the nested formulation with a single-level problem. The key theoretical contribution is to characterize how closely the reformulated function tracks both the values and derivatives of the original outer objective. This connection supports using the reformulation as an optimization target, rather than merely treating it as a convenient substitute.

The resulting SFLCB algorithm uses first-order information in a single loop. Its convergence analysis improves the stated complexity from O(ε⁻³ log(ε⁻¹)) to O(ε⁻³), removing a logarithmic factor relative to earlier double-loop algorithms. Experiments support the theoretical results and the method’s practical efficiency. These conclusions apply to the paper’s structured setting, including the strong-convexity assumption on the inner problem.
neurips-2025-a-single-loop-first-order-a.tldr: SFLCB reformulates a constrained bilevel problem to enable a single-loop, first-order algorithm with an improved convergence bound.

paragraphs: This paper studies targeted adversarial examples that transfer between multimodal models, including models whose internals are inaccessible. Its starting point is that matching only an image’s overall feature representation leaves useful local information unused. Image patches encode finer details, and ignoring them can weaken alignment between an adversarial input and its intended target.

FOA-Attack combines global and local feature matching. A cosine-similarity objective aligns overall representations. For local representations, clustering condenses patch features into compact patterns, reducing redundancy. The method then treats alignment between the adversarial and target patterns as an optimal transport problem, providing a way to match their local feature distributions.

The approach also adjusts the relative influence of multiple models during adversarial example generation. This dynamic weighting is intended to improve transferability alongside the two levels of feature alignment. Across the evaluated models, the authors report stronger performance than existing methods, particularly when transferring attacks to closed-source multimodal models. The findings highlight local feature alignment as a meaningful part of the transferability problem, beyond matching a single global representation.
neurips-2025-adversarial-attacks-against.tldr: FOA-Attack improves targeted attack transfer by aligning both global image features and clustered local features across models.

paragraphs: AutoHood3D supplies a dataset for a concrete engineering problem: automotive hoods deform as trapped fluid and inertial forces act on them during rotary-dip painting. Its more than 16,000 geometric variants give learning systems a broad collection of shapes tied to a shared physical process. The intended uses include component design, process optimization, and models that approximate multiphysics simulations.

Each hood is simulated using coupled fluid and structural calculations, combining Large-Eddy Simulation with Finite Element Analysis and 1.2 million cells in total. The data include physical fields over time, STL geometry files, and structured language prompts for generating geometry from text. This combination connects shape, physical behavior, and language within one benchmark.

The authors validate their numerical methodology and evaluate five neural architectures. Their results expose systematic errors in predicted displacement and force, motivating training objectives that explicitly account for fluid–solid coupling. The benchmark therefore serves both as training material and as a way to identify where learned simulation substitutes fail to capture interacting physics. Reproducible workflows support further model development and benchmark construction.
neurips-2025-autohood3d-a-multimodal-ben.tldr: AutoHood3D connects over 16,000 hood geometries with coupled physics simulations and language annotations to support engineering machine learning.

paragraphs: Offline safe reinforcement learning seeks policies that earn rewards while respecting safety constraints, using an existing dataset. The paper identifies a mismatch in sequence-based approaches: they often represent desired future reward and future cost in the same way. Yet reward is a target that can vary, while the safety budget is a boundary that actions should respect.

Boundary-to-Region, or B2R, changes the interpretation of the cost signal. Under a fixed safety budget, it realigns cost-to-go to represent a constraint boundary and unifies the cost distribution across feasible trajectories while retaining their reward structure. Together with rotary positional embeddings, this design supports exploration within the safe region instead of treating cost as another symmetric performance target.

In experiments, B2R meets safety constraints on 35 of 38 tasks and delivers higher reward performance than the compared baselines. The result supports the usefulness of distinguishing reward goals from safety boundaries in sequence-model conditioning. It also gives a concrete scope to the empirical safety result: constraint satisfaction was achieved on most, rather than all, of the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2025-boundary-to-region-supervis.tldr: B2R conditions offline policies on cost as a safety boundary, meeting constraints on 35 of 38 tasks while improving rewards.

paragraphs: CF-VLM addresses a weakness in vision-language models: a model can match images and descriptions through familiar correlations while missing distinctions that matter for reasoning. The paper uses counterfactual samples to make those distinctions explicit during fine-tuning. The aim is to improve sensitivity to changes that alter the causal meaning of visual and textual content.

The framework combines three training objectives. One preserves basic alignment between images and language. Another reinforces the distinctness and stability of factual scene representations when compared with coherent counterfactual alternatives. The third emphasizes small edits that have important causal consequences. Together, these objectives seek to retain broad cross-modal understanding while making the representation more responsive to consequential differences.

Experiments report consistent improvements over strong baselines and state-of-the-art methods on compositional reasoning and generalization benchmarks. The authors also report promising results for reducing visual hallucinations, suggesting better factual consistency. That latter finding is presented as promise rather than a complete solution. The contribution is a targeted fine-tuning framework that connects counterfactual discrimination with stronger measured reasoning and generalization.
neurips-2025-cf-vlm-counterfactual-visio.tldr: CF-VLM uses counterfactual fine-tuning objectives to improve compositional reasoning and generalization, with promising reductions in visual hallucinations.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts models dynamically route tokens to different expert components. That routing creates a challenge for private inference: the pattern of expert use may itself reveal sensitive information about the input. CryptoMoE addresses this part of the computation, extending cryptographic inference support beyond the dense models emphasized by existing frameworks.

The framework balances workloads across experts to protect routing information and introduces secure protocols for dispatching tokens and combining expert outputs. It also adds confidence-aware token selection and a batch matrix multiplication protocol to improve the accuracy–efficiency tradeoff. These components address both the privacy of dynamic routing and the computational work needed to carry it out.

Experiments on DeepSeekMoE-16.4B, OLMoE-6.9B, and QWenMoE-14.3B report 2.8–3.5-fold lower end-to-end latency and 3–6-fold lower communication than a dense baseline, with minimal accuracy loss. Against an adaptation of CipherPrune for mixture-of-experts inference, communication falls by up to 4.3-fold. The reported results show that protecting expert selection can coexist with substantial efficiency gains in the evaluated models.
neurips-2025-cryptomoe-privacy-preservin.tldr: CryptoMoE protects mixture-of-experts routing while reducing private-inference latency and communication with minimal reported accuracy loss.

paragraphs: When several variables influence an outcome, their contributions can overlap, remain distinct, or depend on acting together. This paper develops a framework for separating those forms of causal influence into redundant, unique, and synergistic components. Its central position is that causal decomposition should be based on interventions, rather than solely on patterns observed in data.

The mathematics draws on Partial Information Decomposition and Möbius inversion. A closed-form expression for the Möbius function of the redundancy lattice makes it possible to systematically separate how causal power is distributed among variables. The purpose is to describe the organization of joint influence, giving more detail than a single measure of an overall causal effect.

The authors illustrate the framework with logic gates, cellular automata, and chemical reaction networks. These examples show that the distribution of causal power can change with context and system parameters. The decomposition therefore characterizes causal contributions in relation to a particular setting. Applications to responsibility attribution, biological networks, and climate models are proposed as possibilities, while the stated demonstrations focus on the three example systems.
neurips-2025-decomposing-interventional-.tldr: The paper decomposes intervention-based causal influence into shared, unique, and synergistic contributions that can vary with context.

paragraphs: A sequence of reasoning steps can sound convincing while containing conclusions that do not follow from earlier claims. GRiD addresses this problem by making the knowledge supporting each step explicit. The paper attributes many such failures to knowledge that remains implicit or insufficiently grounded, leaving dependencies between claims poorly specified.

The framework represents reasoning as a graph with two kinds of nodes: nodes that extract knowledge and nodes that carry out reasoning. Connections record the dependencies between them. A lightweight verifier checks each reasoning step relative to its premises. This structure gives the checking process an explicit account of what a conclusion depends on, rather than relying only on the fluency of the explanation.

Across StrategyQA, CommonsenseQA, GPQA, and TruthfulQA, the authors report substantial improvements in accuracy, consistency, and faithfulness over recent structured reasoning methods. They also find benefits when GRiD is used solely as an inference-time verification module. That result matters practically because the dependency-aware checking component can improve reasoning even without using the entire framework to construct every step.
neurips-2025-dependency-matters-enhancin.tldr: GRiD makes reasoning dependencies explicit and verifies steps against their premises, improving measured accuracy, consistency, and faithfulness.

paragraphs: Steering vectors guide a language model during inference by adding directions to its internal representations. DISCO changes where that intervention happens: it directly modifies the query and value representations inside attention heads. The authors provide evidence that larger portions of these spaces separate concepts linearly than do the output representations of attention heads.

That finding motivates using queries and values as locations for steering. The paper also analyzes how such changes affect attention outputs. It shows that steering an attention head’s input already modifies queries and values, but ties those changes together rigidly. Directly intervening on the two components allows more granular control over effects that the input-level method bundles together.

Experiments on LLaMA 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B compare DISCO with several steering-vector baselines across multiple datasets. The authors report stronger performance, with steering efficacy up to 19.1% higher than the next-best method. The results support query and value spaces as useful intervention points and connect the empirical gains to an analytical account of how steering changes attention.
neurips-2025-disco-disentangled-communic.tldr: DISCO steers attention queries and values directly, enabling finer control and higher measured steering efficacy than compared baselines.

paragraphs: Images and text can describe shared content while also carrying information specific to their own format. DCMEM aims to learn representations that preserve this distinction. The paper identifies two problems in existing multimodal variational autoencoder approaches: weak alignment between modalities and insufficient structure to separate shared information from modality-specific information.

The proposed framework explicitly separates common and distinct factors. Shared representations learned from different modalities supervise one another, encouraging agreement about their common content. An information-bottleneck objective further constrains what the different factors encode, aiming to make them exclusive yet complementary. The intended result is a coordinated representation whose components retain different informational roles.

DCMEM also supports training with both complete and partial multimodal datasets through a valid Evidence Lower Bound, the variational objective underlying the model. Experiments report significant improvements in cross-modal generation, clustering, and classification. These findings connect the representation design to several uses: generating across modalities, grouping related examples, and predicting classes. Support for partial data broadens the training setting beyond datasets in which every modality is always available.
neurips-2025-disentangled-cross-modal-re.tldr: DCMEM separates shared and modality-specific information through mutual supervision and information constraints, improving several cross-modal tasks.

paragraphs: This study asks whether reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards creates new reasoning abilities or makes existing successful reasoning easier to sample. It evaluates multiple model families and training algorithms on mathematics, coding, and visual reasoning. A central measure is pass@k, which examines success when a model receives multiple attempts, including large numbers of attempts.

The evaluated trained models do better with few attempts, but their base models achieve higher pass@k when many attempts are allowed. The authors also observe that the range of solvable problems often shrinks as training continues. Analyses of reasoning-path coverage and perplexity suggest that the trained models’ paths already lie within the base models’ sampling distributions.

These findings support an interpretation of current RLVR as improving sampling efficiency without eliciting fundamentally new reasoning patterns in the studied settings. Treating the base model as an upper bound, the authors find six algorithms similarly underuse its potential. Distillation, by contrast, introduces teacher-derived patterns in their experiments. The paper motivates improved reinforcement-learning paradigms; it does not establish that reinforcement learning could never expand reasoning capabilities.
neurips-2025-does-reinforcement-learning.tldr: The study finds that current RLVR improves access to successful reasoning paths without demonstrating new reasoning patterns beyond the evaluated base models.

paragraphs: Working memory is noisy and limited, so useful behavior depends partly on which information remains precise. This study tests whether rewards shape that allocation. Participants learned associations between stimulus orientations and rewards, then estimated orientations after a delay. The researchers examined both variability in their reports and systematic memory bias.

Memory precision reflected natural stimulus priors as well as reward incentives. Both influences on variability grew over time, consistent with an effect on stabilizing stored representations. Memory bias, however, changed little with time or reward. To interpret this pattern, the authors extended efficient coding theory to include time and an objective of maximizing expected utility. The behavioral findings were consistent with this utility-based account.

Recurrent neural networks trained with different stimulus priors and reward policies showed similar patterns: more probable or more rewarded stimuli were remembered more stably, with differences increasing over time. Transfer-learning experiments identified recurrent dynamics as crucial for adaptation. Together, the behavioral and modeling results support the view that environmental regularities and rewards jointly shape how limited memory resources are allocated.
neurips-2025-efficient-allocation-of-wor.tldr: Human experiments and recurrent networks support working-memory allocation that favors more probable and more rewarding information over time.

paragraphs: A generated video can look convincing frame by frame while its underlying shapes shift inconsistently over time. GeoVideo addresses this gap by adding explicit geometric supervision to latent diffusion video generation. The motivation is that producing realistic two-dimensional appearances alone does not provide a direct mechanism for maintaining coherent three-dimensional structure.

The method augments the generator with depth prediction for each frame. Depth is chosen because of progress in depth estimation and its compatibility with image-based latent encoders. A multi-view geometric loss then aligns the predicted depth maps in a shared three-dimensional coordinate system. This gives the model a training signal that connects structure across frames, alongside its appearance-generation task.

Across multiple datasets, experiments show more stable and geometrically consistent videos than the compared baselines. The reported benefits include better shape consistency, coherence across space and time, and physical plausibility. The contribution is the connection between generated appearance and an explicit depth-based structural constraint, allowing consistency to be encouraged through geometry rather than inferred solely from the visual quality of individual frames.
neurips-2025-geovideo-introducing-geomet.tldr: GeoVideo adds depth prediction and cross-frame geometric alignment to improve the structural consistency of generated videos.

paragraphs: Three-dimensional visual grounding depends on reliable connections between scene observations and annotations. Refer-Judge targets data whose ambiguity or logical inconsistency weakens that supervision. Here, toxic data refers to problematic training examples arising from coarse observations and annotation noise, which can make it unclear what a model should learn from a sample.

The framework uses multimodal language models in a two-stage process inspired by juries and judges. Jurors examine samples from different perspectives and produce structured assessments. Judges combine these assessments using Corroborative Refinement, which adaptively reorganizes the information to address ambiguity caused by biased or incomplete observations. The design makes multiple perspectives part of the data-quality decision.

Experiments report human-level discrimination at the scene level and improved performance for baseline algorithms after data purification. These are complementary findings: the framework can identify problematic examples, and its judgments can improve the supervision supplied to other models. The paper’s contribution is therefore a reasoning-based approach to cleaning 3D grounding data, with measured benefits for both judgment reliability and downstream model performance.
neurips-2025-jury-and-judge-chain-of-tho.tldr: Refer-Judge combines multiple model assessments to identify unreliable 3D grounding data and improve downstream training through purification.

paragraphs: Heuristic search depends on estimates of which states are worth exploring, but learned estimates can be biased by sparse data or incomplete models of the environment. KeeA* asks how search can still use the valuable information within those estimates. It builds on SeeA*, which samples a candidate subset before choosing a node to expand.

The authors first analyze why cluster sampling can outperform uniform sampling in SeeA*, linking the advantage to distribution-aware selection with higher variance. KeeA* then adds cluster scouting and path-aware sampling. These mechanisms use heuristic knowledge to raise the sampling mean and variance, respectively, aiming to produce better extreme candidates from which the search selects.

This approach makes exploration depend on information about available nodes instead of relying entirely on injected randomness. Experiments in retrosynthetic planning and logic synthesis show stronger performance than state-of-the-art heuristic search methods. The theoretical analysis motivates the sampling design, while the empirical results demonstrate its usefulness in the two evaluated application areas. The contribution is a way to guide exploratory sampling even when heuristic estimates are imperfect.
neurips-2025-keea-epistemic-exploratory-.tldr: KeeA* uses imperfect heuristic knowledge to guide exploratory sampling, improving search in retrosynthetic planning and logic synthesis.

paragraphs: Scene text retrieval searches images according to the text they contain. Existing methods often depend on costly bounding boxes marking text locations and struggle to accommodate different query styles within one system. MSTAR addresses both issues by training without box annotations and supporting multiple forms of text queries.

The method progressively builds visual representations that capture text at different levels of detail. Style-aware instructions help accommodate free-form queries, while a multi-instance matching module improves alignment between visual content and language. The authors also introduce MQTR, a benchmark with 16,000 images and four query types, making varied retrieval requirements an explicit part of evaluation.

Experiments cover seven public datasets as well as MQTR. On Total-Text, the authors report a 6.4% improvement in mean average precision over the previous state of the art while removing the need for box annotations. On MQTR, the reported average improvement over previous models is 8.5%. These results support combining lower annotation requirements with a broader query interface, rather than treating query flexibility as a separate retrieval task.
neurips-2025-mstar-box-free-multi-query-.tldr: MSTAR retrieves scene text across multiple query styles without bounding-box supervision and introduces a benchmark for evaluating that flexibility.

paragraphs: Human preferences can differ across people and contexts, but a single reward model can compress those differences into a majority preference. This paper instead learns a distribution over reward functions, each associated with a distinct aligned policy. Disagreement becomes information to represent, rather than a signal that must disappear during aggregation.

The central requirement is pairwise calibration. For each pair of candidate responses, the share of reward functions favoring one response should match the share of annotators who favor it. Training uses pairwise preferences as soft labels without requiring annotator identities or predefined groups. This makes the observed distribution of preferences the direct target of the reward ensemble.

The authors prove that a small outlier-free ensemble can accurately represent diverse preference distributions. They also develop and evaluate a practical training heuristic, reporting improved calibration. That result supports a more faithful representation of pluralistic preferences at the level the method measures: choices between response pairs. The paper connects a formal criterion for preserving disagreement with an empirical method for learning multiple reward functions.
neurips-2025-pairwise-calibrated-rewards.tldr: Pairwise-calibrated reward ensembles preserve preference disagreement by matching how often annotators favor each response.

paragraphs: Attention is a major computational burden in diffusion transformers because its cost grows quadratically as the visual token sequence grows. Sparse attention reduces the number of tokens involved, but very aggressive sparsity can damage image or video quality. Re-ttention targets a specific source of that damage: changes in the probability normalization used by attention.

The method uses redundancy across the diffusion process and information from earlier softmax distributions. It reshapes attention scores using that history so that a small selected subset can better preserve the behavior of full attention. The central idea is to correct the statistical effect of sparsification, rather than relying only on choosing which tokens remain.

Experiments with text-to-video and text-to-image models, including CogVideoX and PixArt diffusion transformers, report operation with as few as 3.1% of tokens during inference. Re-ttention outperforms FastDiTAttn, Sparse VideoGen, and MInference in the stated evaluations. The results support attention-history reuse as a way to sustain visual quality at very high sparsity; the token percentage describes the reported attention sparsity rather than a stated end-to-end speedup.
neurips-2025-re-ttention-ultra-sparse-vi.tldr: Re-ttention uses attention-distribution history to preserve visual quality while reducing inference attention to as few as 3.1% of tokens.

paragraphs: Estimating camera parameters becomes harder when objects move within the scene. Existing approaches often use additional supervision, such as motion masks, known poses, or depth, that casually captured videos do not provide. ROS-Cam estimates camera parameters using a single RGB video as its only supervision, aiming to improve both accuracy and efficiency in dynamic scenes.

The method has three components. Patch-wise tracking filters establish robust, sparse relations across the video. An outlier-aware joint optimization reduces the influence of moving outliers adaptively, avoiding reliance on motion priors. A two-stage optimization strategy improves stability and speed through the design of its loss behavior, including the tradeoff involving Softplus limits and convex minima.

Evaluation includes four real-world datasets and one synthetic dataset. The authors assess camera estimates directly, then use them in a 4D reconstruction method and examine the resulting scenes and rendered color and depth maps. These checks connect camera estimation to the reconstruction it supports. The reported results show more accurate and efficient estimation with RGB video alone as supervision.
neurips-2025-rgb-only-supervised-camera-.tldr: ROS-Cam improves camera estimation in dynamic scenes using only RGB-video supervision and adaptively reducing the influence of moving outliers.

paragraphs: Adding visual inputs gives language models new capabilities but also creates pathways for multimodal jailbreaks. SafePTR starts by investigating where harmful information bypasses safeguards inside these models. The authors report that, in their analysis, fewer than 1% of tokens in early-to-middle layers are responsible for inducing unsafe behavior.

That concentration motivates a selective intervention. SafePTR removes harmful tokens at vulnerable layers, then restores benign features in later layers. The restoration step is part of preserving useful information while suppressing the harmful influence. The framework requires no safety tuning, and the authors report that it adds no computational overhead.

Evaluations span three multimodal language models and five benchmarks. The paper reports state-of-the-art jailbreak mitigation without compromising utility, supporting the value of intervening on a small subset of internal tokens. The significance is both explanatory and practical: the analysis identifies a concentrated source of vulnerability, and the defense uses that finding to target particular layers and tokens. The reported results concern the evaluated models and attacks rather than establishing immunity to every possible jailbreak.
neurips-2025-safeptr-token-level-jailbre.tldr: SafePTR removes a small subset of harmful internal tokens and restores benign features to improve multimodal jailbreak resistance without training.

paragraphs: Two mechanisms in the fruit-fly olfactory circuit are thought to make odor representations easier to distinguish: lateral inhibition and spike frequency adaptation. Because both support pattern separation, they may appear redundant. This paper uses a computational circuit model to examine whether they serve different roles when the amount of environmental noise changes.

The modeled results show different response profiles. Lateral inhibition improves odor discrimination at low and medium noise, but its benefit weakens and can reverse at high noise. Spike frequency adaptation improves discrimination across all tested noise levels. Their relative engagement also changes: lateral inhibition is favored in lower-noise settings, while adaptation dominates when noise is high.

Combining the two sparsification mechanisms produces optimal discrimination performance in the study. This supports a functional explanation for retaining components with apparently similar roles: their usefulness depends on conditions, so their combination supports learning across more complex contexts. The evidence comes from the computational model and its varying-noise tests, showing how context-dependent contributions can make apparent redundancy valuable.
neurips-2025-seemingly-redundant-modules.tldr: A fly olfactory-circuit model shows that two seemingly redundant mechanisms complement each other across different noise conditions.

paragraphs: Synthetic LiDAR scenes are more useful for understanding tasks when their geometry comes with matching semantic labels. Existing range-view generators produce unlabeled scenes, leaving a separate segmentation model to add labels afterward. Spiral addresses the inconsistency that can arise between those separately generated outputs while retaining the efficiency and simpler network design of range-view representations.

Spiral is a diffusion model that jointly generates depth, reflectance, and semantic maps. Bringing these outputs into one generation process makes their relationship part of the modeling task. The authors also introduce semantic-aware evaluation metrics, so assessment considers the quality of labeled range-view data rather than geometry alone.

On SemanticKITTI and nuScenes, Spiral reports state-of-the-art performance with the smallest parameter count among the compared methods. It outperforms two-stage systems assembled from leading generation and segmentation models. The generated range images also improve downstream segmentation training through synthetic augmentation, substantially reducing labeling effort. These findings connect joint generation to both output consistency and a practical use for synthetic labeled data.
neurips-2025-spiral-semantic-aware-progr.tldr: Spiral jointly generates LiDAR geometry, reflectance, and labels, producing useful synthetic training data with strong benchmark performance.

paragraphs: Language-model planning often uses a single agent to generate possible continuations and estimate rewards during Monte Carlo Tree Search. The paper argues that this arrangement can limit exploration because the proposed branches lack diversity. SYMPHONY introduces a pool of agents based on different language models to broaden the reasoning patterns available during planning.

The framework uses this heterogeneity to increase rollout diversity and support more effective exploration. Its central design choice is to coordinate agents with different reasoning tendencies within the planning process. This connects the composition of the agent pool to the variety of candidate paths that search can examine.

Across multiple benchmark tasks, the authors report strong results using open-source models that can run on consumer-grade hardware. Adding cloud models accessed through APIs yields further improvements and surpasses existing state-of-the-art baselines in their evaluations. The findings support heterogeneous coordination as a useful planning strategy across these configurations, with the strongest reported comparisons coming from the version enhanced by cloud-based models.
neurips-2025-symphony-synergistic-multi-.tldr: SYMPHONY coordinates heterogeneous language-model agents to diversify planning rollouts and improve search performance.

paragraphs: Zero-shot time-series forecasting uses past observations as context for predicting future values. TiRex seeks to combine this in-context learning ability with the state tracking associated with recurrent models. The paper argues that conventional LSTMs are well suited to tracking time-series state but lack strong in-context learning, while transformer-based forecasters do not consistently meet expectations.

TiRex builds on xLSTM, an enhanced LSTM with competitive in-context learning capabilities. Its design retains state tracking, which the authors identify as important for long-horizon forecasts. They also introduce CPM, a training-time masking strategy intended to strengthen this ability. These choices link the model’s recurrent structure and training procedure to forecasting over different horizons.

The authors report new state-of-the-art zero-shot results on GiftEval and Chronos-ZS. TiRex outperforms substantially larger models, including TabPFN-TS, Chronos Bolt, TimesFM, and Moirai, across short- and long-term forecasting. The findings support recurrent state tracking combined with stronger in-context learning as an effective architecture choice for the evaluated forecasting benchmarks.
neurips-2025-tirex-zero-shot-forecasting.tldr: TiRex combines xLSTM state tracking with enhanced in-context learning to achieve leading zero-shot forecasting results across short and long horizons.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning needs a reliable way to score model outputs, but demanding visual-perception tasks can be difficult to verify automatically. ViCrit creates a task with a known answer while retaining subtle visual challenges. It starts with a human-written image caption of about 200 words and inserts one small factual error.

The altered words concern objects, attributes, counts, or spatial relationships. Given the image and modified caption, the model must locate the corrupted span. Because the edit is known, an exact-match check supplies a binary reward. The task therefore turns detailed image–text comparison into a training signal that can be verified without an ambiguous judgment about an entire generated answer.

Models trained on ViCrit improve across multiple vision-language benchmarks. Gains extend from natural-image training data to abstract image reasoning and visual mathematics, suggesting transferable perceptual learning rather than only familiarity with seen objects. The authors also introduce ViCrit-Bench, which balances error categories and probes different image domains. Together, the training task and diagnostic benchmark connect fine-grained hallucination detection with broader improvements in visual perception.
neurips-2025-vicrit-a-verifiable-reinfor.tldr: ViCrit trains visual perception through exactly verifiable caption-error localization, with improvements transferring to broader visual reasoning tasks.
